content.text:
I fixed the anchor check in `packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts` so `/docs/php/tooling#phpunit` and `/docs/php/tooling/#phpunit` are now treated the same.

**Why it happened:** the path check already ignores trailing slashes, which is why the error was about anchors and not links. The anchor check didn't. It looked up the target page by its exact pathname. A category index page like `/docs/php/tooling` is stored under `/docs/php/tooling/`, so a link without the slash found no page, and every anchor on it was reported broken.

**The fix:** when looking up the target page for an anchor, the checker now tries the pathname with the slash, without it, and URL-decoded. If any of those matches a page, it then checks whether that page has the anchor.

The existing broken-links tests pass (34/34). I didn't add a test for this case, and I didn't run a full site build to reproduce the reported error.
